pieces.name: Pawn
pieces.description: A low-cost foot soldier that advances toward the opposite edge.
pieces.movement: Moves one square forward, or two from its starting square. Captures one square diagonally forward and promotes on the final rank.

pieces.name: Rook
pieces.description: A heavy line piece that controls ranks and files and can be sacrificed to clear a Barricade.
pieces.movement: Moves any number of clear squares horizontally or vertically. It may sacrifice itself to demolish the first visible Barricade on that line.

pieces.name: Knight
pieces.description: A mobile piece whose unusual route reaches around normal blockers.
pieces.movement: Moves in an L shape: two squares in one direction and one perpendicular. A Barricade blocks jumps that cross its area.

pieces.name: Bishop
pieces.description: A long-range piece permanently tied to one square color.
pieces.movement: Moves any number of clear squares diagonally.

pieces.name: Queen
pieces.description: The strongest standard piece, combining rook and bishop mobility.
pieces.movement: Moves any number of clear squares in any straight direction.

pieces.name: King
pieces.description: The royal piece. Its importance depends on the selected victory rule.
pieces.movement: Moves one square in any direction and may not enter an attacked square.

pieces.name: Maharani
pieces.description: A royal powerhouse combining queen and knight mobility with a controlled 1-blocker jump.
pieces.movement: Moves like a queen or knight. On a queen line it may cross exactly 1 occupied square, but never a Barricade.
rules: Queen movement
Knight movement
May cross exactly 1 blocker

pieces.name: Catapult
pieces.description: A forward siege piece with projectile paths that skip 1 or 2 squares, then recover.
pieces.movement: Moves up to 1 clear square forward or diagonally forward. It captures directly ahead or fires along those three lanes.
rules: Projectile over 1 square: recover for 2 own turns
Projectile over 2 squares: recover for 4 own turns
Barricades block projectiles

pieces.name: Barricade
pieces.description: A neutral wall that blocks movement and projectiles without attacking anything.
pieces.movement: Either player may move it up to 1 clear square when one of their pieces is within 1 square. It cannot capture or be captured normally. A visible Rook may sacrifice itself to remove it.
rules: Neutral
Blocks jumps and projectiles
Controlled by a friendly piece within 1 square
A Rook can sacrifice itself to demolish it

pieces.name: Hypnotizer
pieces.description: A conversion specialist that recruits one adjacent enemy after sustained contact.
pieces.movement: Moves up to 2 clear squares forward or sideways. It cannot move backward or capture normally.
rules: One recruitment target
Kings cannot be recruited
Weak pieces recruit after 3 contact turns
Medium pieces recruit after 4 contact turns
Strong pieces recruit after 5 contact turns
Contact progress resets if separated

pieces.name: Diplomat
pieces.description: A protected peacekeeper that temporarily pacifies nearby enemy pieces.
pieces.movement: Moves up to 1 clear square in any direction. It cannot capture or be captured. After 2 contact turns, it pacifies an enemy for 4 of that enemy's turns.
rules: Uncapturable
Can pacify any enemy piece, including a King
Pacifies after 2 contact turns
Pacification lasts 4 affected-player turns
Retires after 5 pacifications

pieces.name: Cannibal
pieces.description: A shape-stealing piece that consumes pieces behind it, including allies, then borrows their movement for 5 of its own moves.
pieces.movement: Normally moves up to 1 clear square in any direction, but consumes only up to 1 square directly or diagonally backward. After consuming, it uses the victim's movement for 5 Cannibal moves and cannot capture during that form.
rules: May consume allied or enemy pieces only behind it
Borrows the consumed piece's movement for 5 Cannibal moves
Cannot capture while using borrowed movement
Consuming another Cannibal grants Queen mobility
Cannot be revived by Necromancy

pieces.description: A forward-driving heavy piece that moves without capturing or charges through a short lane to remove its occupants.
pieces.movement: Moves forward or sideways up to 4 clear squares without capturing. A charge travels exactly 2 squares and removes every permitted piece on those squares. It never moves backward.

Cannot charge through its own King

Cannot be consumed by a Cannibal

specialAbilities.name: Episcopal
specialAbilities.summary: After 5 own turns, a Bishop may jump horizontally or vertically to any square matching its current board color. Using it starts a 10-turn recharge.
specialAbilities.summaryTemplate: After {initialCooldownTurns} own turn(s), a Bishop may jump horizontally or vertically to any square matching its current board color. Using it starts a {cooldownTurns}-turn recharge.

tunableParameters.label: Recharge
tunableParameters.description: Own turns before another Episcopal jump is available.

detailTemplates: The Bishop may land on any empty square in its row or column that matches the board color beneath it, jumping over ordinary pieces and scorched squares.
It may instead capture an enemy non-King piece on that destination. Kings, allied pieces, Diplomats, protected pieces, Barricades, and scorched squares cannot be targeted.
A Barricade blocks the lane. The jump consumes the turn and must leave the Bishop's King safe.
The first jump becomes available after {initialCooldownTurns} own turn(s), half the configured recharge rounded up. The {cooldownTurns}-turn recharge is shared by every Bishop on that side.

victoryModes.name: Classic Checkmate
victoryModes.summary: Win by checking the enemy King with no legal escape.

victoryModes.name: King Capture
victoryModes.summary: Kings may be captured directly; taking one wins immediately.

victoryModes.name: Timed Match
victoryModes.summary: Each player has a chess clock. Running out of time loses the game.

victoryModes.name: Point Race
victoryModes.summary: The first player to reach the configured captured-piece score wins.

victoryModes.name: Total Elimination
victoryModes.summary: Remove every opposing combat piece; uncapturable Diplomats do not count.

victoryModes.name: Royal Score
victoryModes.summary: Royal defeat ends play, but the player with the higher score wins.

victoryModes.name: Center Dominion
victoryModes.summary: Hold both center squares assigned to your color through the configured number of consecutive opponent turns. The marked center starts empty except for Barricades. Checkmate also wins.

victoryModes.name: Royal Center
victoryModes.summary: Move your King onto any of the four adaptive center squares. The marked center starts empty except for Barricades. Checkmate also wins.

victoryModes.name: Check Race
victoryModes.summary: Be the first player to check the opposing King the configured number of times. Checkmate also wins.

gambit.name: Chass Gambit
gambit.summary: A hidden army-building system that can be combined with custom pieces, board sizes, victory rules, and special abilities.
details: Each player edits only the configured home rows.
Each army must contain exactly one King and stay within its point limit.
Armies remain hidden until both players lock in.
Optional custom rules can add affinity squares and command powers.
draftDetails: Each army begins with its required King already assigned.
Players alternate public selections of the remaining pieces from one shared pool.
A player may lock below the maximum point budget at any time.
After both players lock, each army is arranged privately in its home rows.
